newsitem.title: UK: BOE independence could cost jobs - report.
newsitem.headline: BOE independence could cost jobs - report.

text.p: The decision to make the British central bank independent could hit jobs and output, a study released on Monday said.

Robert Chote, of the Social Market Foundation think-tank, argued that independent central banks usually have to induce deeper recessions to meet their inflation targets than those under direct political control.

"The reformed Bank of England may have a good chance of delivering low inflation by raising interest rates free of political interference, but if the Chancellor did it himself then fewer people would lose their jobs in the process," Chote said.
He said that an extra 50,000 jobs could be sacrificed to keep inflation down to 2.5 percent from the three percent level predicted by the Bank two years from now.
Britain's new Labour government last month gave the central bank independence to set interest rates.
